idiom_name: rust-rule-engine: GRL rule strings over a KnowledgeBase + Facts
implementation_notes: rust-rule-engine brings a Drools/Grule-style production rule system to Rust: rules are written in GRL (rule "name" { when ... then ... }) and loaded into a KnowledgeBase, facts live in a Facts map - or in strongly typed TypedFacts when using the incremental RETE engine - and execution runs through RuleEngine::execute with salience-ordered activation and a no-loop attribute for refraction. The typed RETE API (IncrementalEngine with insert/update/retract and fire_all, plus Templates and global registries) is the variant to prefer when facts have a fixed shape and matching must be incremental. Because rule text is parsed at load time, keep rule strings next to the code and test them like any other input.
pitfalls: GRL field names are strings inside rule text: renaming a fact key breaks rules at parse or evaluate time, so use the typed RETE API (TypedFacts with insert/update/retract) when the fact shape is fixed.
Facts are dynamically typed values: comparing an Integer fact against a Number literal, or reading a missing key, is a runtime error - validate the fact map before running.
An action that asserts the value its condition matches re-activates the rule; without no-loop/salience discipline the agenda can cycle until a limit stops it.
